name: Outdoor ApplianceLinc
description: The outdoor on/off module with RF. Its Get Operating Flags reply holds no documented bits, and it supports only responder links.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

flagCommands.name: programmingLockOn
flagCommands.description: Turns the programming lock on: linking and programming from the device are locked out.

flagCommands.name: ledOnTransmitOn
flagCommands.description: The LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

flagCommands.name: ledOnTransmitOff
flagCommands.description: The LED doesn't blink when the device sends an Insteon message.

flagCommands.name: keyBeepOn
flagCommands.description: The device beeps when a button is pressed.

flagCommands.name: keyBeepOff
flagCommands.description: The device doesn't beep when a button is pressed.

flagCommands.name: radioOff
flagCommands.description: The device doesn't originate RF messages. It still repeats the RF messages it hears.

flagCommands.name: powerLineOff
flagCommands.description: Turns Insteon communication over the powerline off. The device turns it back on whenever it powers up.

flagCommands.name: powerLineOn
flagCommands.description: Turns Insteon communication over the powerline on.

flagCommands.name: x10Off
flagCommands.description: Turns X10 sending and receiving off.

flagCommands.name: x10On
flagCommands.description: Turns X10 sending and receiving on.

flagCommands.name: errorBlinkOff
flagCommands.description: The LED doesn't blink when a communication error occurs.

flagCommands.name: errorBlinkOn
flagCommands.description: The LED blinks when a communication error occurs.

flagCommands.name: checksumOff
flagCommands.description: Extended Set and ALL-Link database write messages needn't carry a checksum in D14.

flagCommands.name: checksumOn
flagCommands.description: Extended Set and ALL-Link database write messages must carry a checksum in D14.

standardCommands.name: lightOn
standardCommands.description: Turns the load on to the level in cmd2 at the saved ramp rate.

parameter.name: onLevel
parameter.description: The level to go to, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full).

standardCommands.name: lightOnFast
standardCommands.description: Turns the load on instantly. The device ignores cmd2.

standardCommands.name: lightOff
standardCommands.description: Turns the load off at the saved ramp rate. The device ignores cmd2.

standardCommands.name: lightOffFast
standardCommands.description: Turns the load off instantly. The device ignores cmd2.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads the load's level. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

standardCommands.name: instantChange
standardCommands.description: Sets the load to the level in cmd2 instantly.

parameter.name: onLevel
parameter.description: The level to go to, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full).

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On-level
responder.description: The on-level; the Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say to set it to 0xFE.

responder.name: rampRate
responder.label: Ramp rate
responder.description: The ramp rate; the Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say to set it to 0x1F.

verification.note: No document says that every nonzero level means on; the ranges are read from the status reply's level byte.

notes: The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes mark the 0x00 reply N/A, so its Set Operating Flags commands have no bit to read back. It sends them as extended messages with a checksum in D14.
The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give no extended Set for the settings its Get reports.
The device sends its Assign to ALL-Link Group broadcast on power-up, and supports only responder links, whose on-level should be 0xFE and ramp rate 0x1F.

The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give the device's identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672 LED bulb; the catalog keeps 0x02 and 0x38 for the 2634-222.

Inferred: seen on two i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48) linked to a Hub 2245, the device itself writes its responder record when it's linked remotely or with the SET button, and takes Data 1 from the load's state at that moment: the two plugs wrote 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on. So Data 1 (on-level) of the load group's responder records is the state the load was in when the device was linked. The On/Off Plug 2635-222 Owner's Manual says to make sure the module is on before linking it as a responder; the Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 Owner's Manual says to set the load to the state the link should recall before linking it as a responder. The 0xFE its link data give is what to write when writing the record by hand.
sources: Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes
